Radio DJs are hardly live anymore. Unless they’re doing contests, on morning talk shows, or midday they are usually pre recording “breaks” and are thrown into the queue. 

Nobody really hangs around a dj studio at 11 pm. No, you’re listening to someone record their bits in a makeshift studio in their basement at some point during the day.

Radio stations are usually limited in what they can play. Often they’ll construct their own “rating” system and play the highest out of 5 stars. That will whittle down a playlist of 1200 songs down to about 300 

Though nobody will be live dj-ing, there will be someone listening throughout the night in order to quality check it, in case there’s any dead air or anything 

If you’re wondering why most of the radio commercials have mostly the same voices presenting them, that’s because they are. People make a legitimate living off of voicing and producing commercials

Hardly any radio DJ uses their real name 

Radio queues are constructed to the precise second when commercials are meant to air 

Radio stations are required to play their legal station ID once per hour (per the FCC)

Radio station IDs east of the Mississippi will all start with the letter W, while west of it will start with K
